summary.headline: Max India Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 66% YoY to INR68.6 crore, but EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore; AGEasy breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR41.3 crore a year ago, though it fell sequentially on lumpy DM fee income. The EBITDA loss was INR25 crore, against INR23.2 crore a year ago and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26, because Q4 included an exceptional DM fee. Antara Noida (340 units) received possession offers in June 2026, with about 75% of dues collected by the call date, though revenue recognition is deferred to Q2 on possession. Management said care home occupancy is improving at 5 of 8 homes and AGEasy's ARR is trending up toward INR120-150 crore, and it reiterated AGEasy profitability by around Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Antara Senior Living (residences)
segments.commentary: Dehradun is profitable and fully occupied; Estate 360 Gurgaon is fully sold out. E361 has sold 154 of 360 units by June end, with 27 sold in Q1 and about 34 in July. Noida possession offers went to 340 residents in June, with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 Care Homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; occupied bed days up 23% QoQ. Occupancy rose at Bannerghatta to 41% (from 37%), Gurugram to 41% (from 33%), Whitefield to 18% (from 8%) and OMR to 12% (from 3%). Four homes reached ARPOB above INR7,000 in June.

segments.name: AGEasy (consumer products)
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR19 crore in Q1, below INR23 crore in Q4 on post-peak moderation. Online gross margin held at 45% (vs 46%). Marketplace ROAS 3.8 and D2C exit ROAS 2.6; marketplace CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically. Monthly revenue run-rate about INR10 crore in July.

segments.name: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR15.75 lakh in Q1 with negative contribution margin; average revenue per client INR4,000, client satisfaction 96%, sessions rose from 199 to 307 in June. Will be built into residences and Care Homes, not as a standalone business.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy expected to reach contribution and EBITDA breakeven around Q4 FY27 (management: 'by January or last quarter of this year'), with CM2 improving as ROAS rises.
AGEasy revenue doubling target for FY27 (from INR77 crore to about INR150 crore) reiterated; management expects significant Q2-Q4 top-line improvement.
Management said it will report a smaller EBITDA loss next quarter versus the 63% figure cited for FY26 (loss to revenue ratio).

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.
Incremental capital requirement of about USD20 million over the next two years (reduced from about USD25 million), with the second fund raise deferred.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida (340 units): possession offers issued June 2026; residents expected to move in over 30-45 days; Phase II approval is the next step, with rates cited at INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft versus INR7,000-10,000 earlier.
Care Homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; all 8 operational after DLF Phase II Gurgaon relaunch in July 2026; each new bed costs about INR10-12 lakh including operating losses.
Chandigarh project unwound after height clearance denial near flight paths post Operation Sindoor.
Second tranche of preference issue of INR40 crore received in July 2026; management says the total capital need is unchanged but working-capital credit lines are being used to bridge timing.
demand_pricing: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity slowed in April-June amid geopolitical uncertainty but recovered in July (34 units) and August; management says it has not seen DLF's senior-living entry affect sales.
AGEasy ROAS improved to 2.0 at Q1 exit from 1.8 in Q4; conversion rate rose from 2% to 3.5% after brand spend (Anupam Kher as ambassador).
AGEasy repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); management's directional target is 20%+.
Management noted that logistics and China-sourcing disruption raised COGS and forced some airlifting, depressing margins.
Competition: management said real-estate developers and hospital chains can replicate infrastructure but not services IP; DLF's launch plans in Gurgaon are reportedly small and tied to Medanta.

qa_highlights.question: What should change in cost and top line by Q4 FY27 for the EBITDA breakeven target, and what are the Care Home bed-addition plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 numbers; breakeven commitment applies to AGEasy, while Care Homes need 8-10 quarters per bed to turn profitable. No new beds are being added now; expansion decision is timed for October-November 2026 subject to occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Blended ARPOB for Care Homes once occupancy rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended ARPOB should be near INR7,500 as recent bed additions were at higher rates.

qa_highlights.question: Bookkeeping: how much of Noida collections is recognised in Q1, and reconciliation of senior living income?
qa_highlights.answer: No Noida revenue was recognised in June; recognition is tied to possession, expected in Q2. Senior living income includes DM fee (about INR7 crore), Dehradun operations (about INR6 crore), finance lease income from re-leasing (about INR15 crore, treated as exceptional) and treasury income (about INR8 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Will AGEasy's INR77 crore to about INR150 crore revenue doubling plan hold given Q1 revenue of INR18-19 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the plan; July run-rate reached about INR120 crore annualised, with Q2-Q4 expected to show significant top-line improvement as ROAS improves.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 AGEasy revenue was seasonal, and what are repeat rate and CAC/LTV indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited festive (Sep-Oct) and winter seasonality plus marketplace year-end deals. Repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); the directional target is 20%+, and ROAS (marketplace near 4, D2C 2.5) is used as the efficiency metric.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from hospital chains, developers and financial players, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued services and IP, not infrastructure, are the moat; hospitals would dilute margins in Care Homes; for AGEasy, moats are senior-specific products (3 patents granted, 3 filed) and brand. AGEasy market potential seen at about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which business gives highest ROCE, and expected cash burn for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: AGEasy expected to have the highest ROCE, followed by Care Homes (about 23-24%+). Management declined to give FY27-28 projections; it said the EBITDA loss ratio fell from 95% to 63% and will fall further next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Capital plan and incremental requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capital need unchanged for two years, reduced from about USD25 million to under USD20 million; incremental requirement about USD20 million. Second fund raise deferred using credit lines; INR40 crore second pref tranche received in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DLF's senior living entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DLF's Gurgaon plan is a small addition within an existing township, reportedly tied to Medanta, and has had no visible impact on Gurgaon sales velocity; it welcomes more players for category awareness.

risks_watch: AGEasy breakeven (contribution and EBITDA) targeted around Q4 FY27 / January 2027; marketplace CM2 at minus 17% in July versus historical minus 70-80%.
Care Home occupancy: 5 of 8 homes on model; expansion decision tied to October-November 2026 occupancy trends.
Noida (340 units) possession and Phase II approval; about 25% of INR169 crore dues still outstanding; revenue recognition shifts to Q2 on possession.
Lumpy DM fee and finance lease income drives quarterly volatility in senior living revenue and EBITDA.
Input cost pressure: China-sourced logistics disruption, airlifting, and labour code manpower cost increase.
Competitive entry by DLF (Gurgaon) and other developers or hospital chains in senior living.
Funding: reliance on working-capital credit lines while second fund raise is deferred; Bangalore project's developer reportedly faced financial issues.
key_quotes: So as you can see now, as the revenue is increasing, the EBITDA losses are now coming down.
AGEasy perhaps by January or last quarter of this year will be in that zone.
So we are not building a INR10,000 crores business in AGEasy in the next 5 years.
But the total number of capital required has not changed for the last 2 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and execution-focused on Noida possession, Gurgaon sales recovery and AGEasy ROAS, but evasive on FY27 and FY28 numerical projections and cash burn. Management repeatedly deferred specific guidance beyond AGEasy breakeven and the Care Home expansion timeline.
